key_insight: A superconducting soliton-based DAC can convert trapezoidal control pulses into precise flux biasing for fast, fixed-time transmon phase gates with CMOS-compatible control.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a scalable way to filter control noise, multiplex qubit control, and implement nanosecond gates while reducing dependence on fragile analog waveform tuning.
method: Trapezoidal drive pulses are transduced into superconducting solitons and stored in a DAC load loop.
The stored soliton generates a controllable flux output that couples to a transmon or gate coupler.
Gate timing and phase can be adjusted via soliton hold time or a DC-biased tunable DAC-qubit coupler.
evidence_signal: Experiments demonstrated 5.6 ns S-gates on transmons with 0.05% per-gate excitation and relaxation below the qubit's intrinsic T1 limit, with simulations matching the observed trends.
watch_item: Scaling to many qubits may be limited by non-local DAC-induced phase errors from electromagnetic interference, even on ancilla qubits not directly coupled to the DACs.
paper_title: Transmon Phase Gates Controlled by Superconducting Soliton DAC
